name: Commercial Robot Vacuum
definition: An autonomous commercial cleaning machine that navigates approved indoor routes and performs dry pickup using brushes and a vacuum airflow path, while staff remain responsible for setup, supervision, debris handling and exceptions.
includedScope: Professional autonomous dry-vacuum robots for commercial interiors
Robots documented for carpet and/or hard-floor dry pickup
excludedScope: Wet pickup or floor scrubbing unless separately documented
Hazardous or combustible dust without exact approval
headline: Commercial robot vacuum airflow, floor tools, navigation, filtration and buyer verification
description: This profile separates dry-pickup hardware from mapping, runtime, public-area safety and fleet-data claims so buyers can compare complete operating systems.
metaDescription: Commercial robot vacuum guide covering navigation, suction and airflow, brushes, filtration, models and procurement checks.
disclaimer: This independent category reference is not a safety, filtration, dust-hazard or purchasing approval. Confirm the exact robot, floor tool, filter, software, mapped site, regional conformity and service plan.

keyFacts.label: Pickup boundary
keyFacts.value: Dry debris pickup through brushes, airflow, separation and containment
keyFacts.evidence: Official sources document roller or side brushes, suction paths and debris containers or bags.
keyFacts.scope: Reviewed robots; not wet pickup or hazardous dust approval.

keyFacts.label: Metric boundary
keyFacts.value: Suction pressure, airflow, cleaning width and pickup result are not interchangeable
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturer sources publish different parameters and test boundaries.

keyFacts.label: Floor boundary
keyFacts.value: Carpet and hard-floor capability depends on the installed floor tool and approved surface
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturers identify different floor surfaces and brush systems.

keyFacts.label: Autonomy boundary
keyFacts.value: Mapping and automatic charging do not remove supervision, emptying or exception work
keyFacts.evidence: Official workflows include mapping, monitoring, charging and manual maintenance.

systemFlow.name: Route setup
systemFlow.evidence: Vendors describe map creation and task scheduling.

systemFlow.name: Surface agitation
systemFlow.componentFamily: Main roller, side brushes and floor tool
systemFlow.role: Moves debris into the pickup path.
systemFlow.evidence: Official pages identify model-specific brush systems.

systemFlow.name: Air transport
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturer sources document suction or airflow systems.
systemFlow.scope: Values are not normalized across brands.

systemFlow.name: Separation and containment
systemFlow.role: Retains collected debris and manages exhaust air.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources identify bags, filters and container capacities.
systemFlow.scope: No universal HEPA result is inferred.

systemFlow.name: Autonomous support
systemFlow.componentFamily: Sensors, battery, charger, alerts and fleet layer
systemFlow.role: Keeps the robot localized and returns work to staff when needed.
systemFlow.evidence: Vendors document sensors, charging and management functions.
systemFlow.scope: Connectivity and service differ by market.

variants.name: Low-profile carpet robot
variants.taskScale: Open commercial carpet and under-furniture routes
variants.operatorRelationship: Staff map, dispatch and empty the robot
variants.spaceConstraints: Transitions, tassels, cables and low furniture require trials
variants.limitations: Low profile does not establish deep-carpet performance.
variants.evidence: Kärcher and ECOVACS position compact commercial vacuum robots for carpeted interiors.

variants.name: Upright multi-surface robot
variants.taskScale: Larger mixed hard-floor and carpet routes
variants.operatorRelationship: Staff select floor tool and maintain bag or bin
variants.spaceConstraints: Height and turning envelope affect access
variants.limitations: Multi-surface claims require each surface to be trialled.
variants.evidence: Gausium and LionsBot document multi-surface systems.

variants.name: Industrial dry-pickup robot
variants.operatorRelationship: Staff establish boundary markers and remove bulk debris
variants.spaceConstraints: Dynamic industrial traffic and drop-offs require control
variants.limitations: Industrial positioning is not combustible-dust approval.
variants.evidence: Makita documents robotic cleaners for commercial or industrial floor areas.

performanceMetrics.name: Cleaning width
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: May include or exclude side brushes
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not compare unmatched width definitions.

performanceMetrics.name: Suction pressure and airflow
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Describe different parts of the airflow system
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Static pressure, airflow and input power are different

performanceMetrics.name: Bin or bag capacity
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Bulk density and fill sensing affect usable capacity.

performanceMetrics.name: Runtime and charging
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Battery, floor resistance and settings dependent
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Maximum runtime is not achieved cleaning time.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Manufacturers publish model-specific runtime or charging data.

performanceMetrics.name: Practical coverage
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Measures completed route output under real conditions
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Must include turns, obstacles, emptying and interventions
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not mix vendor theoretical and site-measured values.
performanceMetrics.evidence: LionsBot labels practical efficiency while other sources use different descriptions.

applicationFit.evidence: Kärcher, ECOVACS and LionsBot position robots for carpet cleaning.
applicationFit.scope: Approved carpet type and floor tool.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Pickup, pile interaction, edge result and visible grooming should be trialled together.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Run seeded-debris and full-shift trials on representative carpet.

applicationFit.evidence: Gausium and LionsBot document multi-surface use.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Transitions and tool compromises can matter more than nominal suction.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Measure pickup and autonomous behavior across every transition.

applicationFit.evidence: Makita positions DRC models for large commercial and industrial floor areas.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Traffic segregation, bulk debris and dust classification determine fit.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Approve debris class, routes and interaction with vehicles.

componentStack.name: Floor tool and brushes
componentStack.role: Agitate surfaces and feed the pickup inlet.
componentStack.evidence: Official sources show model-specific brush systems.

componentStack.name: Airflow and containment
componentStack.role: Transports, separates and retains dry debris.
componentStack.evidence: Manufacturers document different containers and filters.

componentStack.name: Navigation and safety
componentStack.role: Localizes, plans paths and responds to people or obstacles.
componentStack.evidence: Official product pages describe different sensor stacks.

componentStack.name: Battery and charger
componentStack.role: Supplies traction, vacuum and computing power.

componentStack.name: Fleet and service layer
componentStack.role: Schedules, reports and supports the robot.
componentStack.evidence: Gausium and LionsBot document fleet-management features.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Pickup, grooming, edges and intervention rate
procurementDecisions.assessment: Judge completed clean routes and visible outcome together.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Run repeatable seeded-debris and full-shift trials.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm tool, brushes, airflow path, bag or bin and software.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Filter classification, system leakage and emptying method
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating a filter label as whole-machine performance
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources describe filters but not one common system test.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Require evidence for the complete air path and maintenance method.
procurementDecisions.basis: Containment depends on seals and handling.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Obtain test basis and assess exposure during emptying.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify filter, seals, bag or bin and approved dust class.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Traffic response, noise, warnings and recovery workflow
procurementDecisions.evidence: IEC and vendors define autonomous controls and operating limits.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Approve site behavior under peak traffic and changed layouts.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Document site risk assessment and exception ownership.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Test obstacles, glass, drops, blocked routes and emergency stops.

engineeringChecks.reason: Brush and inlet geometry determine surface interaction and pickup.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Confirm exact tool and consumable IDs for each surface.

engineeringChecks.reason: Filter media alone does not define whole-machine containment.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Obtain system test basis and approved dust class.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturer sources describe filters and bags.
engineeringChecks.scope: Non-hazardous use unless exact approval exists.

engineeringChecks.reason: The robot moves around people, obstacles and level changes.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Verify conformity documents and site controls.
engineeringChecks.evidence: IEC 63327 covers automatic commercial floor-treatment machines.

engineeringChecks.reason: Uptime depends on the full support system.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Record versions, battery pack, charger, spares and SLA.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official sources document charging and fleet functions.
